title: Big Campaign Numbers Need a Closer Look
summary:
Can a number be correct but still leave something important out? A fact-check published by PBS NewsHour shows why election claims need a closer look.

President Donald Trump is campaigning for Republican candidates before elections that will decide which party controls Congress. PolitiFact examined statements from his speeches and interviews.

One claim said $22 trillion in foreign investment was coming into the United States. PolitiFact found that the White House website listed $11.2 trillion, about half that amount. Even that smaller total included plans stretching over several years and some purchases or sales, rather than money already invested.

Another claim said more Americans were working than ever before. The report says employment did reach a record of more than 159 million people in August. But a growing population helps explain that record. Other measures of how many people are working were not at record levels.

Prices also tell a mixed story. The report says groceries overall had become more expensive, while eggs and bread had become cheaper.

The useful question is not just how big a number sounds. It is what the number actually measures.
why_it_matters: The same number can be understood differently when its dates, measurement and limits are missing.
